title: Anthropic's IPO is just the beginning
excerpt: Should you invest in Anthropic? We break down everything you need to know ahead of the AI giant's IPO.
content_html:
By Dan DeFrancesco

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

Executive Editor and lead writer for BI Today

2026-11-19T11:21:57.343Z

Here. We. Go.

Anthropic's first day of trading marks a seminal moment for the AI industry. The AI giant's IPO means an industry built on private-market potential faces public-market scrutiny.

Even up until the last minute before its big debut, Anthropic has continued to outperform expectations. Wednesday night, it priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the $70 to $78 range it had initially set.

We don't know for sure when Anthropic will begin trading, but we're covering it all on our live blog. Follow along here.

Let's get the first big question out of the way: Should you invest in Anthropic?

Investing in a company on IPO day usually isn't a great bet. But Anthropic isn't just any company. It's the market's first crack at a pure-play AI business.

Maybe that's why when we asked five investing pros for their thoughts, the responses were pretty mixed.

Still have questions? You're in luck. We're hosting a live Q&A at 1 p.m. ET. I'll be joined by First Trade's Joe Ciolli, AI Insider's Alistair Barr, and Sarah E. Needleman, our senior leadership and workplace correspondent. We'll be chatting all things Anthropic and the wider AI industry.

The impact of Anthropic's IPO won't stop when the trading day ends.

If anything, it's just the beginning.

First and foremost, a lot of people are going to get rich. At the top of that list are Anthropic's seven cofounders with their multi-billion-dollar stakes. There are also the other 5,000-plus Anthropic employees, many of whom will turn into multimillionaires. We've compiled a list of who stands to gain the most.

Selling shares will be a bit more complicated than usual, though. BI's Stephen Council previously reported on Anthropic's unique structure to avoid insider trading. (And don't forget about that tax bill!)

That money could land in some interesting spots. (And not just pumping up a chaotic San Francisco housing market.)

A massive liquidity event can spawn more new companies. Employees cash out and look to start their own thing. (See: the PayPal Mafia.)

Meanwhile, VCs are also happy to take their winnings and start looking for the next Anthropic to invest in.

So while today is the end of Anthropic's journey as a startup, it's the beginning of a bunch of others.

Dan DeFrancesco
